_about: Extra lines for the Practice door, lessons, games and the grown-ups gate (stream C). Built by tools/make_bix_extra.py into audio/bix-extra-<voice>.js. Same rules as bix_lines.json: no names, short and kind.
door_ask: How do you want to play with numbers?
path_here: This is your skill right now! Tap Learn it with Bix.
path_done: You already know this one. Great job!
gate_grownup: This part is for a grown up. Go get a grown up!
build_go: Make this number on the abacus!
learn_beads: The top bead is worth five. Each bottom bead is worth one. A bead counts when it touches the bar.
learn_add_direct: When there are enough beads, just push them up to the bar. No tricks yet!
learn_sub_direct: If the beads are already at the bar, just push them away.
learn_sf_add: Not enough little beads? Use the five bead, and take away its small friend. Small friends make five.
learn_sf_sub: Need to take away, but the little beads are not there? Take away the five bead, and add back its small friend.
learn_bf_add_a: No room on the rod? Add ten on the next rod, and take away the big friend. Big friends make ten.
learn_bf_add_b: Same trick with smaller numbers. Add ten, and take away the big friend.
learn_bf_sub_a: Not enough beads to take away? Take ten from the next rod, and add back the big friend.
learn_bf_sub_b: Same trick with smaller numbers. Take ten, and add back the big friend.
learn_combined: Sometimes the big friend needs a small friend inside it. Two tricks, one move!
learn_two_digit: Work left to right. Tens rod first, then the ones. Every rod uses the same friends.
learn_anzan: Picture the beads in your head. Move them in your mind, and say the answer.
learn_long_rows: Long rows use every friend you know. Keep going, number after number, and let the beads do the thinking.
learn_rows_2d: Five big numbers in a row. Tens rod first, then the ones.
learn_anzan_more: Same beads in your head, more numbers. Keep the picture still between numbers.
learn_three_digit: Now three rods for each number: hundreds, tens, and ones. Always start on the left.
learn_times_a: Three times four means three fours: four, eight, twelve. Count up on the abacus, then learn it by heart.
learn_times_b: The bigger tables! Three times seven is three sevens: seven, fourteen, twenty one.
learn_anzan_2d: Picture two rods now, tens and ones. Add the tens first, then the ones.
learn_four_digit: Four rods for each number now. Left to right, one rod at a time. Every friend still works.
learn_mul_2x1: Start at zero. Go left to right. Times each digit by the small number, and add the answer to the abacus.
learn_mul_3x1: Same trick, one more digit. Hundreds, then tens, then ones.
